pluss::note::format¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::format(string_view tpl,
                         std::initializer_list<Binding> bindings)

Fill A Template, Get A Scalar Note¶

format() renders a template string against a set of named bindings and returns the result as a scalar (dim=0) UTF-8 Note — one cell holding the finished string. It is the assembly counterpart to the splitting factories: where from_lines and from_words break a string apart, format builds one up.

Use it whenever a string has to be built from named parts: a labelled message, a generated identifier, a one-line report, a path or query. Beyond plain substitution it also evaluates a small expression language inside each placeholder, so light computation — arithmetic, choices, list joins, a bound callback — can happen in the template instead of in the surrounding code.

The result is a scalar Note and never larger; format produces a single string, not a column. To build many strings, call it per row, or use the vectorised Note methods on an existing Note.

Bindings¶

Each entry in bindings is a Binding — a name paired with either a value or a callable:

{"user", "Ada"}                       // string value
{"count", 42}                         // integer value
{"ratio", 0.75}                       // floating-point value
{"ok", true}                          // bool value
{"tags", std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b"}}   // list value
{"shout", [](std::string s) { return s + "!"; }}  // callable

Value bindings accept bool, any signed or unsigned integer, any floating-point type, char, const char* / std::string_view / std::string, and std::vector<T> (which becomes a list). Binding names must be non-empty and unique across the list.

Template Syntax¶

  • Text outside { } is copied verbatim.

  • {{ emits a literal {; }} emits a literal }.

  • { name } substitutes the value of binding name.

  • { expression } evaluates the expression and splices in its stringified result.

The Expression Language¶

Inside { } the following is available, loosely in C++ spelling:

  • Literals — integers and decimals (42, 3.14, 1e3); string literals in '...' or "..." with \n, \t, \\, \", \' escapes.

  • Identifiers — a bare name is that binding’s value; :: qualified names are allowed (used by the built-in functions).

  • Arithmetic — + - * / and unary + - !. Arithmetic is done in floating point; an integer-valued result prints without a decimal point.

  • + on non-numbers — string concatenation, after stringifying each side.

  • Comparisons — <  <=  >  >= compare numerically; == and != compare the stringified operands.

  • Logic and choice — &&, ||, and the ternary cond ? a : b. Truthiness: non-zero numbers, non-empty strings/lists, true.

  • Indexing and members — x[i] and x.at(i) take a list element or a one-character slice of a string; x.size() and x.empty() work on both strings and lists.

  • Built-in functions — std::abs / std::fabs, std::sqrt, std::floor, std::ceil, std::round, std::pow(a, b), std::min(...) / std::max(...) (two or more arguments), std::accumulate(list, init), pluss::join(list) or pluss::join(list, delimiter) (default delimiter ", "), and std::to_string(x) / pluss::str(x).

  • Callable bindings — { fn(args...) } invokes a bound C++ callable. Arguments are converted to the callable’s parameter types; the return value is stringified. A callable binding used without () is an error, and a value binding used with () is an error.

How Values Stringify¶

true / false for bools; plain decimal for integers; up to 15 significant digits for floating point (so 5.0 prints as 5, 2.5 as 2.5); [a, b, c] for a list.

Example 1: A Plain Substitution¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::format("Hello, {name}!", {{"name", "Ada"}})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"Hello, Ada!"

The result is a scalar Note — the finished string in one cell.

Example 2: Literal Braces¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::format("{{literal}} and {x}", {{"x", 7}});
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"{literal} and 7"

{{ and }} are the escapes for literal braces; {x} still substitutes.

Example 3: Arithmetic In The Template¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::format("{a} + {b} = {a + b}", {{"a", 2}, {"b", 3}})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2 + 3 = 5"

{a + b} is evaluated; the integer-valued result prints as 5, not 5.0.

Example 4: Division Keeps The Fraction¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::format("{p / q}", {{"p", 10}, {"q", 4}});
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2.5"

Arithmetic is floating point, so 10 / 4 is 2.5.

Example 5: String Concatenation¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout, pluss::note::format(
    "{greet + ' ' + who}", {{"greet", "hi"}, {"who", "there"}})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"hi there"

+ with non-numeric operands joins them; ' ' is a string literal inside the placeholder.

Example 6: A Ternary Choice¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::format("{n > 1 ? 'many' : 'one'}", {{"n", 5}})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"many"

Example 7: Boolean Logic¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::format("{ok && n == 3}",
                                          {{"ok", true}, {"n", 3}});
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"true"

== compares the stringified operands; the && result stringifies as true.

Example 8: Indexing And .size() On A List Binding¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::format(
    "first={xs[0]} count={xs.size()}",
    {{"xs", std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b", "c"}}})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"first=a count=3"

Example 9: A Built-In Function¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::format("{std::sqrt(x)}", {{"x", 16}});
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"4"

Example 10: Variadic std::min / std::max¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::format(
    "{std::min(a, b, c)}/{std::max(a, b, c)}",
    {{"a", 4}, {"b", 1}, {"c", 9}})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"1/9"

Example 11: Joining A List¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::format(
    "{pluss::join(xs, '-')}",
    {{"xs", std::vector<std::string>{"x", "y", "z"}}});
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"x-y-z"

Without the second argument, pluss::join uses ", ".

Example 12: Reducing A Numeric List¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::format(
    "{std::accumulate(xs, 0)}",
    {{"xs", std::vector<int>{1, 2, 3, 4}}})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"10"

The second argument is the initial value.

Example 13: A Callable Binding¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::format(
    "{shout('hi')}",
    {{"shout", [](std::string s) {
        for (auto& ch : s) ch = std::toupper(ch);
        return s + "!";
      }}});
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"HI!"

The string literal 'hi' is converted to the lambda’s std::string parameter; the return value is spliced in.

Example 14: A Missing Binding Is Rejected¶

try {
  pluss::note::format("{absent}", {{"x", 1}});
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

pluss::note::format: missing binding 'absent'

Example 15: An Unmatched Brace Is Rejected¶

try {
  pluss::note::format("{x", {{"x", 1}});
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

pluss::note::format: unmatched '{' in format template

Use {{ for a literal {.

Example 16: A Duplicate Binding Name Is Rejected¶

try {
  pluss::note::format("{x}", {{"x", 1}, {"x", 2}});
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

pluss::note::format: duplicate binding 'x'

Binding names must be unique.

  • pluss::note::select: choose among prepared strings by boolean conditions instead of rendering one.

  • pluss::note::from_lines / pluss::note::from_words: the inverse direction — take a string apart.
